summary: This lecture tells the story of the boy, the monk and the king who claimed to be God, the story of Ashab al-Ukhdud, which took place before the Prophet Muhammad SAW was born and which he himself told his companions. The ustaz says it is in Sahih Muslim. A boy being trained as the palace sorcerer meets a monk who follows Prophet Isa AS and learns to know Allah, and Allah gives him the ability to heal people. The monk and the minister who believed are killed, but the boy survives the mountain and the sea until he himself teaches the king how to kill him by saying the name of the boy's Lord. Many people believed, the king dug a trench of fire, and the story is recorded in Surah Al-Buruj. The ustaz closes by linking it to Abraha's arrival in Yemen.
keyPoints: The story was told by the Prophet SAW himself and, the ustaz says, is in Sahih Muslim.
The boy learned tawhid from a monk even though he was meant to become the king's sorcerer.
Allah gave the boy the ability to heal people, and he used it to call people to Allah.
The monk and the minister were killed for refusing to give up their faith, but Allah saved the boy from the mountain and the sea.
The boy himself showed how to kill him by saying Allah's name, and many people then believed.
The story of those burned in the trench is recorded in Surah Al-Buruj and is linked to why Abraha was in Yemen.

chapters.title: Opening and the source of the story
chapters.summary: The story took place before the Prophet SAW was born and was told by him; it is in Sahih Muslim.

chapters.title: The king who claimed to be God, and his sorcerer
chapters.summary: The king used a sorcerer to deceive the people. When the sorcerer grew old, he asked for a boy to be trained to succeed him.

chapters.title: The boy is chosen and meets a monk
chapters.summary: A boy of about 12 or 13 was chosen, and on his way to the palace he came across a monk who followed Prophet Isa.

chapters.title: The monk teaches tawhid
chapters.summary: The monk taught that only Allah is worshipped, not people or statues, and the boy stopped by to learn every day.

chapters.title: Scolded by both sides, and the monk's idea
chapters.summary: The boy was scolded by the sorcerer and by his parents for being late, so the monk gave him an idea.

chapters.title: A beast blocks the road
chapters.summary: A huge beast blocked the road, and the boy wanted to know whether the monk or the sorcerer was right.

chapters.title: The stone and the boy's prayer
chapters.summary: The boy prayed to Allah and threw a small stone, and the beast died.

chapters.title: The monk's warning: you will be tested
chapters.summary: The monk said the boy was now better than him, warned that he would be tested, and told him not to reveal where the monk was.

chapters.title: Healing people and calling them to Allah
chapters.summary: Allah gave the boy the ability to heal, and he taught people that Allah heals, not magic.

chapters.title: The blind minister and the refused gifts
chapters.summary: The king's blind minister came with gifts, but the boy refused them and said Allah is the one who heals.

chapters.title: The minister believes and the king is furious
chapters.summary: The minister believed and was healed. When the king heard that the minister's Lord was Allah, he tortured the minister and arrested the boy and the monk.

chapters.title: The monk and the minister are killed
chapters.summary: The king had the monk and the minister sawn in two for refusing to give up their faith, but the boy still said there is no god but Allah.

chapters.title: The boy survives the mountain and the sea
chapters.summary: The boy was taken to a mountaintop and out to sea, but he prayed to Allah and he alone survived.

chapters.title: How to kill the boy, and the people believe
chapters.summary: The boy taught the king to tie him up and shoot him with an arrow saying Allah's name, and many people declared faith in the boy's Lord.

chapters.title: The trench of fire and Surah Al-Buruj
chapters.summary: The king dug a trench of fire for those who would not give up their faith. The ustaz recites Surah Al-Buruj and tells of a mother with her baby.

chapters.title: Closing and the link to Abraha
chapters.summary: One man escaped to Sham, the king of Abyssinia sent an army, and Abraha, who became king in Yemen, was in that army.

books.context: The ustaz says this story is in this hadith collection, one of the two most important.
Mentioned with Sahih Muslim as the two books that gather the sayings and actions of the Prophet SAW.

people.context: Made the people worship him and killed the monk and the minister. The ustaz says the king's name is not important.
Deceived the people for the king and, when old, asked for a boy to be trained to succeed him.
About 12 or 13 years old, he learned tawhid from the monk and called people to Allah with his ability to heal.

people.role: Follower of Prophet Isa AS who taught tawhid
people.context: Taught the boy to worship only Allah, and was killed by the king for not giving up his faith.
Believed and regained his sight, then was killed by the king for not giving up his faith.
The ustaz says the monk followed Prophet Isa because Prophet Muhammad SAW had not yet been born.

people.role: A king who also used sorcerers
people.context: Mentioned as a comparison with the king in this story.

people.role: King who sent an army to Yemen
people.context: Sent an army to defeat the wicked king after a man who escaped reported the events in Sham.

people.role: General who became king of Yemen
people.context: Was in the Abyssinian army and later became king in Yemen, and eventually came to attack Mecca.

lessons.title: Only Allah is worshipped
lessons.body: The monk taught that no human can be made a god and statues made by people cannot be worshipped. Only the one Allah.

lessons.title: An honest teacher admits his student's strength
lessons.body: The monk told the boy he was now better than him and reminded him to be ready to be tested.

lessons.title: Those given a gift will be tested
lessons.body: The monk warned that a gift from Allah comes with a test.

lessons.title: Use your skills to call people to Allah
lessons.body: The boy used his ability to heal to call people to Allah. Those who can draw, sing, practise martial arts or speak well can do the same.

lessons.title: Allah is the one who heals
lessons.body: The boy refused the minister's gifts and stressed he could not heal anyone. Allah heals.

lessons.title: The monk hid, not out of fear
lessons.body: The monk told the boy to keep his place secret so he could keep teaching, but when arrested he showed his confidence in Allah.

lessons.title: Standing firm in faith
lessons.body: Even after seeing the monk and the minister killed before his eyes, the boy still said there is no god but Allah.

lessons.title: Entrusting matters to Allah in prayer
lessons.body: On the mountain and at sea the boy prayed that Allah deal with them in whatever way He wished, and Allah saved him.

lessons.title: The aim of calling to Allah is people's salvation
lessons.body: The boy did not want to be famous, rich or a king. He wanted everyone to become Muslim and enter paradise.

lessons.title: The truth is in the end recognised by many
lessons.body: After the boy was killed with Allah's name on the king's lips, everyone declared belief in the boy's Lord.

glossary.meaning: A boy, here about 12 or 13 years old.
A religious teacher who lives apart praying and teaching, likened by the ustaz to an imam.
Knowledge taught by Satan, which the king used to deceive the people.
The sayings, actions and conduct of the Prophet SAW collected in the hadith books.
The testimony that there is no god but Allah, which the minister said when he accepted Islam.
The people killed in the trench, mentioned in Surah Al-Buruj.
The name of a surah. The ustaz says it means something very high, like the Burj Khalifa.

dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW told that there was once a king who had a sorcerer. When the sorcerer grew old, he asked for a boy to be taught. The boy met a monk who taught him tawhid, and Allah gave him the ability to heal people. The king tortured and killed the monk and the minister who believed, but Allah saved the boy from the mountain and the sea. In the end he showed how to kill him by shooting an arrow while saying the name of the boy's Lord, so the people believed and the king dug a trench of fire.
dalil.context: The ustaz says this story was told by the Prophet SAW himself and is in Sahih Muslim. He does not name the narrator.
The ustaz recites the opening of Surah Al-Buruj.
dalil.translation: By the sky with its towering constellations,

dalil.context: The second verse of Surah Al-Buruj, recited by the ustaz.
The third verse of Surah Al-Buruj, recited by the ustaz.
dalil.translation: by the Witness and that which is witnessed,

dalil.context: The verse that mentions the people killed in the trench, Ashab al-Ukhdud, which the ustaz says is this very story.
dalil.translation: damned were the makers of the trench,

sirah.era: Before the Prophet's birth: a story of earlier peoples
sirah.summary: This lecture tells a story of an earlier people that the Prophet SAW related: the boy and Ashab al-Ukhdud. It is linked to why Abraha was in Yemen before the Year of the Elephant.
